Question: What is the selection process of the UPSC selection post recruitment?
Old_Answer: Step 1: Scrutiny of the application is done by the UPSC to see if you meet the eligibility criteria (both education and/or experience) Step 2: A list of shortlisted candidates is published on the UPSC website and a chance is given to the un-shortlisted candidates to make representations if they think they should have been included. They can write and email to the UPSC. Step 3: The UPSC can hold a written examination for the post depending on the number of candidates. The written test is always followed by an interview. Else, there is only an interview. Step 4: UPSC conducts the interview at UPSC Bhawan, New Delhi. The scrutiny criteria is generally quite peculiar for specific posts and number of vacancies is also mostly quite low.

Question: How do you deal with being rejected for a promotion you actually think you deserved?
Old_Answer: I work with the Government of India. I will get my promotion only when my senior retires, which is 8 years from now. I will be eligible for it in 3.5 years. I will still have to wait another 4.5 years and there’s absolutely nothing I can do about it. So, I just accept the fact that there is. If I were in my previous job, it would have taken me around 25 to 30 years to reach where I am today. I could only get here because I tried to make a switch to a better position and it did require a lot of courage. We often tend to start feeling comfortable in a secure place. So, my way to deal with delayed promotions is to trying to do my best to get to a better position through hard work. I can leave it to time but I can also try harder. However, no pressure about it. Things take time. Luck also has to be on one’s side. I can’t affect all the factors but only the very few that are in my control. I’ll be happy if I get to a better place and even if I don’t. I have come to believe happiness has much little to do with designation than we assume.

Ultimately, maintaining a positive outlook and treating setbacks as stepping stones can empower you to keep striving for your goals. Remember, the path to success is rarely linear, and sometimes the delays can lead to even greater opportunities down the line.
